description: Risk R-B first, because the class name inverts the behaviour: the prompt-mandated Java class for COTRN01C is TransactionAddController, and this program adds nothing - it VIEWS. Four independent artefacts say so: app/cbl/COTRN01C.cbl:5 'Function    : View a Transaction from TRANSACT file', README.md:314 '| CT01 | COTRN01 | COTRN01C | Transaction View |', app/bms/COTRN01.bms:2 'CardDemo - Transaction View' and the on-screen literal INITIAL='View Transaction' at POS=(4,30). The mapset corroborates it structurally: 56 DFHMDF entries, 21 named, and exactly ONE UNPROT - TRNIDIN at :85 - which is a lookup-then-display screen and not a data-entry screen. Rule R1 resolves the conflict - the name comes from the prompt, the behaviour comes from the source - and practice B4 governs the disclosure, so it is documented here and never silently corrected. ON THIS PATH THE MISLEADING NAME IS AT ITS MOST DANGEROUS, AND THE WARNING IS THE POINT OF THIS PARAGRAPH. The condition this case forces is a DUPLICATE KEY, and a duplicate key arriving at a class called 'Add' is exactly the signal that tempts an implementer into insert semantics: a duplicate is what a WRITE reports when the record is already there, so the reflex is to treat it as a failed insert and either retry, upsert or fall back to a rewrite. THERE IS NO INSERT ANYWHERE IN THIS PROGRAM. The statement at :269-278 is a keyed EXEC CICS READ, the duplicate is reported BY THAT READ, and the program's entire response is to display the two response codes, set a message and repaint an empty form. No write expectation is authored here and none may ever be: expectedWrites is empty as a positive assertion, and the adapter additionally verifies on EVERY case that no mutating repository method was reached, so the claim is enforced mechanically rather than merely stated. The half of the swap that genuinely ADDS a transaction is COTRN02C, and its cases live in parity/COTRN02C. WHAT THIS CASE PINS: the WHEN OTHER arm of EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD at app/cbl/COTRN01C.cbl:289-295, reached from the REENTER plus DFHENTER path by the outcome common.FileStatus names DUPLICATE and maps to the batch status '22'. It is the THIRD and last arm of that evaluation, and it is the only one of the three that emits a DISPLAY - :290 is the ONLY DISPLAY statement in all 330 lines of the program. case08 pins the first arm, DFHRESP(NORMAL); case09 and case05 pin the second, DFHRESP(NOTFND); case10 pins this third arm via the '10'-mapped END_OF_FILE outcome, and THIS case pins the same arm via the '22'-mapped DUPLICATE outcome. It is deliberately case10's near-clone: the seeded data, the request, the trace, the screen, the navigation, the message text and the pinned clock are all identical, so that the ONE thing that differs - the RESP/RESP2 pair and the FileStatus mapping it corresponds to - is the only thing a failure here can be about. That isolation is the entire diagnostic value of having both cases. GATE G47 READ HONESTLY, AND WHY NO BRANCH IS INVENTED. The gate asks that every FileStatus and RESP outcome - '00', '10', '22', '23' and other - be driven per call site. COTRN01C has exactly ONE I/O call site: the keyed EXEC CICS READ ... UPDATE at :269-278. Its EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD at :280 has exactly THREE arms and no more: DFHRESP(NORMAL) at :281, DFHRESP(NOTFND) at :283 and WHEN OTHER at :289. A keyed READ cannot report a duplicate as a distinct COBOL branch - the source enumerates no duplicate condition, and there is no alternate-index browse here to enumerate one for - so the '22' outcome legitimately COLLAPSES into WHEN OTHER. This case supplies the '22'-mapped outcome and asserts that it lands in WHEN OTHER, because that is what the COBOL does. It deliberately does NOT add a duplicate-specific message, does NOT add a fourth arm to the evaluation, and does NOT add any recovery, retry or fallback behaviour: the gate is satisfied by proving each outcome reaches its CORRECT arm, and a fabricated branch would satisfy the letter of a checklist while asserting a control flow the source does not have (practice B4 - document, never invent). The collapse is stated openly here rather than papered over (practice B12). The translation reaches the same reading independently: TransactionAddController.readTransactFile documents that 'a duplicate and an end-of-file both reach WHEN OTHER, because the source enumerates neither'. THE TRACE, statement by statement, and identical to case10's apart from the response the read reports. :88-92 sets ERR-FLG-OFF and USR-MODIFIED-NO and blanks WS-MESSAGE and ERRMSGO. EIBCALEN is 218, so :94 takes its else arm and :98 copies the passed area over CARDDEMO-COMMAREA. CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT arrives at 1, so CDEMO-PGM-REENTER already holds at :99 and control takes the ELSE at :110-111 - which is why the echoed context is still 1 and why the :100 SET, the :101 MOVE LOW-VALUES TO COTRN1AO and the :102 MOVE -1 never run. :111 performs RECEIVE-TRNVIEW-SCREEN (:230-238), then the ordered EVALUATE EIBAID at :112 takes its FIRST arm, WHEN DFHENTER, and performs PROCESS-ENTER-KEY. The EVALUATE TRUE at :146 takes its SECOND arm - TRNIDINI is populated, so it is neither SPACES nor LOW-VALUES - and that arm is MOVE -1 TO TRNIDINL (:154) followed by CONTINUE, with no message and no send. WS-ERR-FLG is therefore still 'N', so :158 IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON is TRUE: the thirteen detail items are blanked in source order at :159-171 (TRNIDI, CARDNUMI, TTYPCDI, TCATCDI, TRNSRCI, TRNAMTI, TDESCI, TORIGDTI, TPROCDTI, MIDI, MNAMEI, MCITYI, MZIPI), :172 moves TRNIDINI into TRAN-ID and :173 performs READ-TRANSACT-FILE. The read at :269-278 states DATASET ('TRANSACT') INTO(TRAN-RECORD) LENGTH(LENGTH OF TRAN-RECORD) RIDFLD(TRAN-ID) KEYLENGTH(LENGTH OF TRAN-ID) UPDATE RESP RESP2, and reports the '22'-mapped duplicate outcome. The EVALUATE at :280 therefore falls past both named arms to WHEN OTHER, whose five statements run in this exact order: DISPLAY 'RESP:' WS-RESP-CD 'REAS:' WS-REAS-CD (:290), MOVE 'Y' TO WS-ERR-FLG (:291), MOVE 'Unable to lookup Transaction...' TO WS-MESSAGE (:292-293), MOVE -1 TO TRNIDINL (:294) and PERFORM SEND-TRNVIEW-SCREEN (:295). Control returns to the END-IF at :174, and :176 IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON is now FALSE - a second test rather than an ELSE - so the thirteen record-to-screen moves at :177-190 and the send at :191 are SKIPPED. The task ends at the EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID(WS-TRANID) COMMAREA(CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) of :136-139. THE MAP IS SENT EXACTLY ONCE. The unconditional PERFORM SEND-TRNVIEW-SCREEN at :109 belongs to the first-entry arm and is unreachable from the :110-111 else arm, so on the REENTER path the only send is the rejecting one inside the read. case05 reaches its arm from :103-107 and then falls through to :109, which is why its fingerprint carries two sends; a fixture asserting two sends here would be describing that case rather than this one, and the count is behaviour rather than bookkeeping. ALL THIRTEEN DETAIL FIELDS ARE SPACES, not LOW-VALUES and not record data: they were blanked at :159-171 before the read and the error flag then blocked :176, so nothing ever repainted them. This is the assertion that matters most on a duplicate-key outcome, and it is subtler here than on case10's end-of-file. A duplicate arm CARRIES A RECORD - CICS returns the first match alongside the warning, and common.FileStatus.Outcome.DUPLICATE is one of the only two outcomes for which TransactionRepository.ReadResult permits a record to be present at all - so the record for the requested key genuinely is in the translation's hand when WHEN OTHER runs. The COBOL still never paints it, because the record-to-screen moves live behind the :176 guard that the error flag has just closed. A translation that reasoned 'the record is available, so show it' would paint all thirteen fields and fail on every one of them at once, and that is precisely the divergence this case exists to catch. TRNIDINO retains the requested id, because COTRN1AO REDEFINES COTRN1AI so the received TRNIDINI occupies the same sixteen bytes and no arm of this path clears them. THE DISPLAY LINE, BYTE-EXACT - the distinguishing assertion of this case. :290 is DISPLAY 'RESP:' WS-RESP-CD 'REAS:' WS-REAS-CD. The two literals are exactly 'RESP:' and 'REAS:' - five characters each including the colon, with NO space after either colon - and they are reproduced character for character. WS-RESP-CD and WS-REAS-CD are both PIC S9(09) COMP (:43-44), and DISPLAY of a binary item renders it at its declared digit positions, so each operand is exactly NINE digits, zero-filled on the left, and the whole line is 5 + 9 + 5 + 9 = 28 characters with no separator anywhere. The rendering is therefore 'RESP:000000015REAS:000000000', and a reviewer can check the arithmetic from the two declarations alone (practices B8 and B12). THE PINNED PAIR IS RESP 15 AND RESP2 0, AND THE MAPPING IS NAMED RATHER THAN LEFT IMPLICIT. 15 is common.FileStatus.DUPKEY, the CICS DFHRESP(DUPKEY) face of the batch FILE STATUS '22' that FileStatus.DUPLICATE carries; FileStatus.outcomeOfCicsResp(15) returns Outcome.DUPLICATE, and Outcome.DUPLICATE carries FileStatus.DUPLICATE, which is the two-character status '22'. That is the whole chain from the forced response to the '22' this case claims to pin, and every link in it is a constant in common/FileStatus rather than an assumption. 0 is FileStatus.NO_REASON_CODE, which is what CICS sets RESP2 to for a condition that carries no qualifying reason - reporting zero says 'the condition had no further reason', which is a true statement about what is known, whereas inventing a non-zero reason code would put a number where CICS's own reason code belongs. The same DUPLICATE/15/0 triple is already the established convention in this fixture tree, at parity/COUSR01C/case08.json. Neither value is 0 for RESP - that is DFHRESP(NORMAL) and belongs to case08 - neither is 13 - that is DFHRESP(NOTFND) and belongs to case09 and case05 - and neither is 20, which is DFHRESP(ENDFILE) and belongs to case10. Both values are PINNED CONSTANTS and neither is derived from anything run-variant (practice B7). WHY DUPKEY AND NOT DUPREC, since both spell the batch status '22'. common/FileStatus documents DUPREC = 14 as 'a record with that key already exists on WRITE' - a condition a WRITE reports, and this program issues no WRITE anywhere - and DUPKEY = 15 as 'another record with the same alternate key exists', which is the read-side spelling and the one CICS returns alongside the record rather than instead of it. A duplicate observed BY A READ is therefore DUPKEY, and that is what is pinned. Both values map forward onto '22' and the reverse direction is deliberately ambiguous in FileStatus for exactly that reason, so the case names the response it forces instead of relying on the status to imply it. Note also the numbering trap this does NOT fall into: FileStatus.LENGERR is the CICS response 22 while FileStatus.DUPLICATE is the batch status '22', and the two are unrelated values from two independent numbering schemes. EXACTLY ONE ENTRY carries this DISPLAY, and it is the ONLY entry on the DISPLAY_LINE channel. It is ORDERED THIRD rather than first, and the position is a fact about the fingerprint rather than a preference: the recorder reports WS-MESSAGE at its declared PIC X(80) first, ERRMSGO at its declared PIC X(78) second, and every DISPLAY after them, and the differ compares emitted lines POSITIONALLY and on their declared channels. Placing an 80-byte expectation opposite a 28-character observation would compare across channels of different widths, which is precisely the comparison the channel model exists to prevent, so the DISPLAY is stated where it is emitted in the fingerprint and its uniqueness is asserted by there being one of it. THE ERROR MESSAGE, BYTE-EXACT, AND DELIBERATELY NOT SPECIALISED. The literal at :292-293 is 'Unable to lookup Transaction...' - lower-case 'lookup', capital 'T' in 'Transaction', three trailing dots - reproduced character for character with no normalisation. It is thirty-one characters, and it is identical to case10's because the source moves the SAME literal for every WHEN OTHER outcome: the arm does not know or care which condition sent it there, and a duplicate-key-specific message would be an invented one (practice B5). It is asserted on both channels at their own widths because :217 moves WS-MESSAGE PIC X(80) into ERRMSGO PIC X(78) and COBOL discards the two rightmost bytes: WS_MESSAGE_80 carries the literal followed by 49 spaces and SCREEN_ERRMSG_78 the same literal followed by 47, both counted mechanically rather than by eye (practice B11). This is not either of the program's other two message literals and must never be confused with them: case09 and case05 report 'Transaction ID NOT found...' from :285-286, case06 reports 'Tran ID can NOT be empty...' from :149-150, and case17 and case18 report CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY from :130. All three are distinct, and only this one accompanies a DISPLAY. THE SEEDED RECORDS, AND WHY THE REQUESTED KEY MUST BE PRESENT. TRANSACT has no ASCII fixture - app/data/ASCII holds exactly nine files and none is a transaction master - so the rows are declared inline and no tenth fixture is invented. Three rows are seeded, and row 2 IS the requested id 0000000000001002. On this case that presence is a REQUIREMENT rather than a flourish: a duplicate outcome carries a record, TransactionRepository.ReadResult enforces that a record is present exactly on the normal and duplicate arms, and the only honest source for those 350 bytes is a row the case itself seeded. Forcing a duplicate against data that did not contain the key would mean inventing a record no copybook, no fixture and no case declared, and every field of the resulting screen would then be compared against an expectation derived from nothing. So the record the operator asked for is PHYSICALLY PRESENT, the read reports a duplicate-key condition over it, and the run must still take WHEN OTHER, emit the DISPLAY, leave the thirteen detail fields blank and send once. 0000000000001001 and 0000000000001003 bracket it one below and one above, so a repository that fell to a neighbouring record would also be caught. Each row is 350 bytes, summed mechanically from the fourteen spans of app/cpy/CVTRA05Y.cpy (practice B11): TRAN-ID X(16) 1-16, TRAN-TYPE-CD X(02) 17-18, TRAN-CAT-CD 9(04) 19-22, TRAN-SOURCE X(10) 23-32, TRAN-DESC X(100) 33-132, TRAN-AMT S9(09)V99 133-143, TRAN-MERCHANT-ID 9(09) 144-152, TRAN-MERCHANT-NAME X(50) 153-202, TRAN-MERCHANT-CITY X(50) 203-252, TRAN-MERCHANT-ZIP X(10) 253-262, TRAN-CARD-NUM X(16) 263-278, TRAN-ORIG-TS X(26) 279-304, TRAN-PROC-TS X(26) 305-330 and FILLER X(20) 331-350. The FILLER is present and space-filled (gate G21): it is a span rather than a gap, and omitting it would leave every row 330 bytes. TRAN-AMT occupies ELEVEN bytes - nine integer digits and two fractional, scale 2 (gate G23) - with the sign OVERPUNCHED into the trailing byte 143 and never carried in a twelfth byte or a leading sign position: '0000010011A' is +1001.11 because A is the positive overpunch for 1, '0000010022B' is +1002.22 because B is the positive overpunch for 2, and '0000010033L' is -1003.33 because L is the negative overpunch for 3. PIC X spans are space-padded and PIC 9 spans zero-filled. Both timestamps of every row are PINNED 26-byte literals in the YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.mmmmmm shape - 4+1+2+1+2+1+2+1+2+1+2+1+6 = 26 - and never a captured 'now' (practice B7). None of the record content is ever painted on this path, which is the assertion; the projection of a record that IS painted is case08's subject. THE ONLY NON-RESP DIFFERENCE FROM case10, DISCLOSED RATHER THAN LEFT FOR A READER TO FIND. Row 2's TRAN-DESC prose reads '... THE READ REPORTS THE 22-MAPPED OUTCOME' where case10's reads '10-MAPPED' - two bytes, at offsets 103-104, inside the TRAN-DESC X(100) span. It is retargeted because leaving case10's text in a case that forces the '22' outcome would state something false about this fixture, and a fixture that misdescribes itself is worse than one that differs by two bytes. The span is inert on this path: TRAN-DESC is never painted, because the error flag closes the :176 guard before the record-to-screen moves, so the change cannot affect the screen, the message, the DISPLAY, the cursor, the navigation or the return code. Everything else about the three rows - every other span of every row, both timestamps, all three overpunched amounts and the FILLER - is byte-identical to case10. TRANSACT'S FINAL STATE IS PINNED UNCHANGED, and that is an assertion rather than bookkeeping. :275 states the UPDATE option, so the read takes a record lock, and a translation that took the lock and then rewrote or deleted the record would be caught here and nowhere else in the response. This matters more on a duplicate than on any other outcome: a duplicate is the one failing condition that still hands the translation a usable record and a held lock at the same time, which is the exact circumstance in which an upsert or a de-duplicating rewrite would look reasonable to someone reading the class name instead of the source. The repository returns the failure as a DISCRIMINATED OUTCOME carrying the status with its RESP and RESP2 and NEVER abends on the caller's behalf, which is what lets the COBOL's own EVALUATE structure survive the translation unchanged; an exception would have unwound past :176 and lost the second test altogether, and the DISPLAY with it. The keyed read is a READ ... UPDATE that never rewrites, the repository correctly declares no rewrite and no delete for TRANSACT, and the ADD(YES) and DELETE(YES) flags on app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD:81-82 are capabilities the program does not use rather than behaviour to reproduce (practice B5). THE HIGHLIGHT, and a finding this fixture records rather than invents. Gate G38 asks that the CSSETATY error highlight apply only in REENTER state. This case is REENTER AND in error, which is the combination in which a highlighting screen would highlight - and COTRN01C still applies none, because it has no highlighting to apply. The program's eight COPY statements at :52-72 are COCOM01Y, COTRN01, COTTL01Y, CSDAT01Y, CSMSG01Y, CVTRA05Y, DFHAID and DFHBMSCA: CSSETATY is NOT among them, the source contains zero occurrences of DFHRED and no FLG-<field>-NOT-OK pair for a resolver to act on, and no attribute byte is moved anywhere in its 330 lines. COTRN01C therefore satisfies G38 in the strongest available form - no highlight in EITHER state - and 'attributes' is present and EMPTY rather than absent, which is the positive statement that the decision was taken through the same FieldAttributeSetter the highlighting screens use and came back untouched. Pinning DFHRED and a '*' on TRNIDIN would assert an attribute byte this program never writes, on a path where it never writes it, and that is exactly the invention practice B4 forbids. METADATA IS NOT PAYLOAD. The xxxL, xxxF and xxxA items of app/cpy-bms/COTRN01.CPY are length, flag and attribute metadata and never payload members, which is why none of them appears among the twenty-one fields; note also that this symbolic map declares that TRIAD and no xxxC, xxxP, xxxH or xxxV item at all, so there is no attribute quad here to encode even had the program written one. TRNIDINL is the metadata item that matters here: -1 is moved into it twice on this path, at :154 and again at :294, and -1 in an xxxL item is the CURSOR request, so it is reported once as cursorField exactly as AAP section 0.3.9 requires. STATELESSNESS (rule R6, gate G37): the whole 218-byte area travels in the payload and nothing is held server-side. app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy is 34 + 84 + 12 + 16 + 14 = 160 bytes and the CDEMO-CT01-INFO extension at :53-61 is 16 + 16 + 8 + 1 + 1 + 16 = 58, which is 218 in all; the 58-byte extension is carried as its own field rather than folded into the 160-byte context all seventeen controllers depend on, and all 22 fields are pinned so none is left unchecked. The AID travels in the payload too. The case supplies a realistic re-entry - the operator arrived from CT00/COTRN00C on page 1 of a browse spanning 1001 to 1003, selected 1001, and has now typed 1002 over the field - and every one of those values comes back exactly as it arrived, because no arm of this path writes a CDEMO- field. CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT remains 1. CDEMO-CT01-TRN-SELECTED carries 0000000000001001 deliberately: it is read only at :103-107 inside the first-entry arm and must NOT be consulted here, because :172 keys the read from the TYPED TRNIDINI, so a translation that reached for the commarea selection instead would be keying 1001 and not 1002. A field the passed area does not name keeps what its picture gives it, spaces for PIC X and zeros for PIC 9. NAVIGATION AND TERMINATION. There is NO EXEC CICS XCTL on this path, so no transfer target is invented and the XCTL of :205-208 stays unreached - which is why gate G40 is not asserted here. nextProgram nonetheless carries COTRN01C, and that is not a transfer: the task ends at EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID(WS-TRANID) and app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD:429-430 binds TRANSACTION(CT01) to PROGRAM(COTRN01C), so the operator's next input returns to this same program and the response says so rather than leaving the client to guess. nextMapset and nextMap carry the COTRN01 and COTRN1A that the SEND at :219-225 names, and termination is RETURN_TRANSID. THE RETURN CODE IS 0: COTRN01C contains zero CALL 'CEE3ABD' sites, so a duplicate-key condition on a lookup is a screen error rather than an abend - the operator is told, the transaction returns normally, and gate G35 does not apply. No abend expectation is stated, because inventing one would turn a reported failure into a terminated task. THE HEADER SIX come from POPULATE-HEADER-INFO at :243-262 and are identical on every send this program makes. TITLE01O is CCDA-TITLE01 PIC X(40) from app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy:18-19 and TITLE02O is CCDA-TITLE02 PIC X(40) from :22 - the ACTIVE line, because :21 is COMMENTED OUT in the copybook and carries the superseded 'Credit Card Demo Application (CCDA)' text that must not be used. Neither is COTTL01Y's X(40) CCDA-THANK-YOU at :23-24, and neither is CSMSG01Y's X(50) CCDA-MSG-THANK-YOU at :18-19; the two thank-you items are different widths in different copybooks and are not interchangeable. TRNNAMEO is WS-TRANID 'CT01' X(04) and PGMNAMEO is WS-PGMNAME 'COTRN01C' X(08), both from :36-37. CURDATEO and CURTIMEO are built from FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE at :245 and are therefore the one part of the screen a wall clock would make irreproducible, so the clock is PINNED at 2022-07-19T23:12:34 - the timestamp the source's own version footer at :329 carries, 'Date: 2022-07-19 23:12:34 CDT' - giving CURDATEO '07/19/22' from WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY and CURTIMEO '23:12:34' from WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS. The same pinned pair is used by case01 through case10, so a header difference between sibling cases can only mean a difference in the header logic (practice B7). BASELINE PROVENANCE (practice B12): every expected value here is STATICALLY DERIVED, by structured reading of MAIN-PARA, PROCESS-ENTER-KEY, READ-TRANSACT-FILE, SEND-TRNVIEW-SCREEN and POPULATE-HEADER-INFO cross-checked against the copybook byte layouts (app/cpy/CVTRA05Y.cpy, app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy, app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy, app/cpy/CSDAT01Y.cpy, app/cpy/CSMSG01Y.cpy), the BMS field contract (app/cpy-bms/COTRN01.CPY and app/bms/COTRN01.bms) and the file and transaction definitions in app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD:76-77 and :429-430. The twenty-one field widths come from the symbolic map's xxxI PICTURE clauses and the three record images from the copybook's span table, both computed rather than typed by eye, and every length was measured programmatically. It was NEVER captured from a live COBOL execution: running the legacy programs is empirically impossible in this environment, which AAP section 0.7.6 establishes with eight independently verified blockers, and the change of provenance is escalated as risk R-A rather than absorbed silently. DFHAID and DFHBMSCA are IBM-supplied and absent from this repository (risk R-D), so the DFHENTER this case names is the mnemonic common.CicsAid reproduces from IBM CICS documentation, and the DUPKEY value 15 is likewise a documented CICS response reproduced in common.FileStatus rather than read from a DFHRESP copybook this repository does not contain. NO USER RULES WERE PROVIDED for this project - review_rules returns exactly one line, 'No user rules provided.', and that is the entire document - so no rule is cited here because none exists, none is invented, and the absence is not treated as licence to lower the bar (AAP section 0.10). The AAP section 0.10.2 practices bind in their place, and the ones this fixture is held to are named at the point they apply: B1 (no placeholder anywhere), B3 (app/cbl, app/cpy, app/cpy-bms, app/bms and app/csd are read only), B4 (risk R-B and every divergence disclosed, never corrected), B5 (no invented write, retry, abend or duplicate-specific message), B7 (the clock, the RESP/RESP2 pair and both record timestamps are pinned), B8 (US-ASCII named explicitly, every field fully padded, the DISPLAY rendering and the FileStatus-to-RESP mapping stated rather than implied), B11 (widths from the PICTURE clauses, the 80-to-78 truncation and the 350-byte spans counted mechanically) and B12 (provenance and the G47 collapse stated openly). GATES DISCHARGED: G15 (one of exactly twenty cases in parity/COTRN01C), G18 (the diff count must be zero, per module rather than per build), G19 (three 350-byte records, each pinned as a whole image so the total width is asserted), G21 (FILLER present and space-filled at 331-350), G23 (all three amounts are scale 2 with the sign overpunched into byte 143), G30 (both ordered EVALUATEs honoured in source order - EIBAID at :112 takes the first of its five arms, and WS-RESP-CD at :280 reaches WHEN OTHER only after DFHRESP(NORMAL) and DFHRESP(NOTFND) have both been tested and failed, which is what makes WHEN OTHER genuinely last rather than merely written last), G37, G38 (REENTER WITH error, and still no highlight, because this program has none), G47 (the '22'-mapped DUPLICATE outcome of the single keyed read, landing in WHEN OTHER and reported as a discriminated value rather than an exception) and G51 (the controller is driven as a plain object, with no MockMvc, no TestRestTemplate, no servlet container and no HTTP in the path). Deliberately NOT asserted, because this program or this path has none of them: G32 (zero GO TO in COTRN01C), G35 (zero CALL 'CEE3ABD', which is why the return code is 0 and no abend is expected), G39 (no pagination), G40 (no XCTL on this path) and G43 (no 9300-CHECK-CHANGE-IN-REC). COTRN01C performs no arithmetic at all - zero ADD, SUBTRACT, COMPUTE, MULTIPLY and DIVIDE - and ROUNDED appears zero times in it as in all 28 programs, so any scaling is RoundingMode.DOWN by rule R2. Dead working storage is left exactly as it stands (practice B5): WS-USR-MODIFIED at :45-47 is set at :89 and never tested again, and WS-TRAN-DATE PIC X(08) VALUE '00/00/00' at :50 is never referenced at all; neither is asserted, and neither is tidied away.
